name: Solgrip Cardamom-Rose Pulls
description: Long-pull taffy-style chews with a floral cardamom-rose core that blooms slowly as you work the synth-base. Each strip is hand-twisted by micro-batch machines in the Tier 2 Wicker corridor.
flavor_profile: Warm cardamom up front, followed by a deep rose finish with a faint powdery sweetness and a waxy, satisfying chew
slogan: Pull it slow. Let it open.
cultural_context: A staple of corner kiosks in the lower Shelf districts, Solgrip Pulls are associated with long transit commutes — something to work through a 45-minute mag-rail ride. Older Tier 2 residents sometimes call them 'grandma candy' with affection.
story_hooks: A Shelf-born courier always carries a strip of Solgrip as a personal ritual before a dangerous run — a runner they're tracking does the same, and it becomes an unexpected point of recognition.

A black market chemist has been lacing a specific batch of Solgrip Pulls with a mood-suppressing compound — subtle enough to pass undetected, but affecting an entire transit corridor's population over weeks.
A Tier 4 food critic writes a viral piece calling Solgrip 'the most honest candy in Meridian 88,' causing a sudden demand spike that threatens to price out the Shelf residents it was made for.
